strings.name: Lee Chong Wei
strings.role: Badminton singles player · Three-time Olympic silver medallist
strings.summary: Lee's speed, net control and counterattacking kept him among the world's leading men's singles players. Three consecutive Olympic silvers and rivalries with Lin Dan and others expanded badminton's Asian and international following. He received a doping sanction in 2015, though the panel found no intent to cheat, and retired in 2019 after treatment for nasopharyngeal cancer. He later supported badminton through youth events and public activity.

strings.influence.rationale: A long-serving world number one and Olympic medallist who profoundly influenced Malaysian and international badminton.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Three consecutive Olympic silvers
strings.highlights.h1.text: Reached the men's singles finals in 2008, 2012 and 2016.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Trained in Penang under coaches including Teh Peng Huat, then with Misbun Sidek in the national team.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Sustained elite competition
strings.highlights.h2.text: Repeatedly held the number-one ranking and advanced Malaysian badminton through sustained performance.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Developing the Lee Chong Wei Cup
strings.timeline.t1.text: After its inaugural youth event, outlined a future plan for international expansion in 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: BWF Hall of Fame induction
strings.timeline.t2.text: Joined Lin Dan at the formal Kuala Lumpur induction ceremony.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announced retirement
strings.timeline.t3.text: Ended competition after treatment for nasopharyngeal cancer in 2018.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Third Olympic silver
strings.timeline.t4.text: Reached another singles final in Rio.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Doping sanction
strings.timeline.t5.text: Received an eight-month ban backdated from August 30, 2014 to April 30, 2015; the panel found no intent to cheat, but a violation remained.
strings.timeline.t6.title: London Olympic silver
strings.timeline.t6.text: Reached his second Olympic singles final.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Beijing Olympic silver
strings.timeline.t7.text: Reached his first Olympic singles final and first became world number one that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First Malaysia Open title
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won men's singles at the major home international tournament.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Joined the national team
strings.timeline.t9.text: Progressed from Penang's training system to Malaysia's national squad.
